title: Classical first-order deduction across formula presentations

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Syntax and semantics of predicate logic; Natural Deduction (handout 8)
Proofs and Types (web reprint 2003, corrected 1990 edition)

summary: Translate classical first-order deductions between full connective trees and the existing abbreviated syntax, preserving scope and auxiliary names.
abstract: Conjunction can be written as a negated implication in classical logic, but a proof using that abbreviation still needs to reproduce the usual conjunction rules. We derive those rules, the corresponding disjunction rules and the fresh-witness rule for existential quantification inside the full classical calculus. They let us translate deductions between the full formula alphabet and the smaller established one. The translations preserve assumptions, term substitution and temporary names. Every full formula is classically interderivable with its expansion, although the two formula trees can differ; the same comparison then applies to proofs from arbitrary sets through their finite supporting assumptions.
